title: Nokia
extract:
Nokia is a Finnish telecommunications company. It began in 1865 when mining engineer Fredrik Idestam opened a wood pulp mill in southern Finland, later moving operations near the Nokianvirta river, which gave the company its name.

== Mobile phones ==
Through the 1990s and 2000s Nokia became the largest maker of mobile phones in the world, with models such as the 3310 selling in huge numbers. At its peak in the late 2000s it held roughly 40 percent of the global handset market.

== Decline ==
Apple introduced the iPhone in 2007 and Google's Android followed. Nokia's Symbian software struggled to compete with touchscreen-first platforms. In 2010 Nokia appointed Stephen Elop, a former Microsoft executive, as chief executive. In February 2011 an internal memo by Elop compared the company to a man standing on a burning oil platform. Days later Nokia announced it would adopt Microsoft's Windows Phone as its main smartphone platform.

== Sale to Microsoft ==
In September 2013 Microsoft announced it would buy Nokia's devices and services business. The deal closed in April 2014. Nokia refocused on network equipment and in 2016 completed its acquisition of Alcatel-Lucent.
